title: The Mind and the Palm Leaf
label: ch:sa-mind-verbs
canDo: I can say that someone thinks, understands, reads and writes in Sanskrit; I can name the class that plants -अय- inside a verb, build "understands" out of a prefix and a verb I already had, say what लिख् meant before it meant write, and tell a word worn down by speech (तद्भव) from one carried over whole (तत्सम).

payoff.summary: Say लिखति, give the scratching sense its root carried first, run the chapter's four verbs back as root plus class plus ending — the planted -अय- of चिन्तयति, the अव- prefix and the waking बुध् behind understanding, the plain -a- of पठति and लिखति — sort Bengali lekhā and Hindi cintā into तद्भव and तत्सम, and name the two word-histories that needed a label rather than a claim.
